item.title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78503-y

In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.

item.title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78585-8

Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice.

item.title: A prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids
item.description:
Ryan T. Lingg, Shane B. Johnson, Dalton C. Hinz, Abdullahi A. Mohamed, Timothy D. Skog, Manuela Lizarazu, Sara A. Romig-Martin, Ryan T. LaLumiere, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78719-y
Abstract Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. The prevailing view is that stress-induced increases in glucocorticoids underlie the enhancement of memory consolidation, strengthening memories and promoting their generalization—referred to here as the standard model. However, circuits that drive memory consolidation often also regulate glucocorticoid release, confounding whether their effects on memory are circuit-driven or hormonally mediated. Here we identify a prefrontal pathway that controls memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids. Using optogenetic manipulations in male rats, we found that post-training inhibition of the rostral prelimbic cortex (rPL) to anteroventral bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) pathway promoted contextual generalization in an inhibitory avoidance discrimination task without affecting memory strength. Although this manipulation further elevated corticosterone, it produced generalization even in adrenalectomized rats, demonstrating glucocorticoid independence. Conversely, post-training pathway excitation enhanced contextual discrimination. Recordings of calcium signals revealed context-specific engagement of both avBST and avBST-projecting rPL neurons during memory retrieval, with greater responses in the neutral than the aversive context. These findings reveal glucocorticoid-independent circuit control of memory specificity, setting boundary conditions on the standard model and demonstrating mechanistic heterogeneity that may inform stress-related disorders where memory generalization is a core feature.

item.title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
item.description:
Viacheslav Korolev, Thomas Lettau, Vipin Krishna, Alexander Croy, Martin Thümmler, Michael Zürch, Christian Spielmann, Maria Wächtler, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78716-1
Abstract High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron–phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron–phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

item.content:encoded:

Model simulations show that the 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a substantially longer and more intense event under comparable present-day conditions.

item.title: Short-term effectiveness and impact of Vaxchora vaccine during the 2024 cholera outbreak in Mayotte
item.description:
Antoine Brault, François Herry, Sara Mazzilli, Lina Cristancho-Fajardo, Margaux Froidefond, Mathieu Epinoux, Melissa Berot, Marion Soler, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78733-0
Abstract Global cholera resurgence and vaccine shortage have driven the adoption of reactive one-dose strategies with killed oral cholera vaccines (OCVs). The live-attenuated vaccine CVD 103-HgR (Vaxchora) shows high efficacy in human challenge studies, but its real-world effectiveness in outbreaks is unknown. Here, we analyze the 2024 outbreak in Mayotte, focusing on Koungou village, which had high cholera incidence and vaccine uptake. We develop several stochastic models and calibrate them to daily cases by vaccination status. In total, 3354 individuals (71%) of Koungou’s at-risk population ( n = 4733) received CVD 103-HgR, and 77 cases were confirmed, with symptom onset between 19 April and 7 July 2024. At baseline, we estimate a basic reproduction number $${R}_{0}$$ R 0 of 1.5 (95% credible interval (CrI): 1.2, 1.9) and a CVD 103-HgR effectiveness in preventing cholera of 87% (95% CrI: 74, 99), remaining between 75% and 91% across scenarios. Counterfactual simulations estimate 536 (95% CrI: 240, 824) cases averted at baseline, with a range of point estimates from 152 to 1228 across sensitivity analyses. Rapid single-dose CVD 103-HgR deployment is associated with high effectiveness during a real‑world outbreak, with a substantial but more uncertain population impact, supporting the inclusion of live-attenuated OCVs in reactive strategies when necessary.
